intent: remote SDK settings for claude-sdk boxes: the app sets model/effort from the bot settings panel via the nested text-payload control family (set_name, set_push_preview, set_job_completion_push — and now set_sdk_config), the box validates with the SAME caps as the welcome-metadata identity fields, persists the knobs into the shared state-dir .env (the mergedEnv source LoadSDK and the supervisor's respawn re-resolution both read), answers on a NEW transient per-device frame sdk_config_result, then bounces the harness through the existing supervisor restart control. Confirmation is NOT a new frame: the post-restart welcome / agent_state identity carrying the new model IS the confirmation (the SDK session --resumes across the bounce). Non-claude-sdk harnesses refuse. Old apps never send the control; on an old box the ride degrades to a literal JSON text message reaching the harness — the family's standing fail-open. Old apps ignore the unknown sdk_config_result t. HOT-APPLY AMENDMENT (SC6–SC9): a MODEL-only change on a hot-capable box applies to the LIVE SDK session (the harness's Query.setModel through the box→harness sdk_apply notification) with NO restart — the box defers the result until the harness confirms, persists AFTER the ok, and answers restart:false hot:true; confirmation is the next agent_state snapshot carrying the new model (the wire never drops, no welcome). EFFORT HOT AMENDMENT: effort hot-applies exactly like model (applyFlagSettings/setMaxThinkingTokens on claude-sdk, setThinkingLevel on pi), so the hot gate is 'forwarder bound AND (model or effort present)' and the restart path is now ONLY the forwarder-unbound fallback for older binaries (SC9).

assertions.statement: set_sdk_config rides as a nested text control: a NORMAL device_send whose 'send' text payload is the serialized control object; a box that recognizes the t consumes it silently at the inbound boundary — never delivered to the harness, never a transcript/journal event, no sent echo, no error frame.

box-side validation is authoritative and uses the welcome-metadata caps (WM1/WM2): model is '' (clear) or ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$ (<= 64 chars); effort is '' (clear) or, lowercased and trimmed, one of low|medium|high|xhigh|max or a positive integer string, <= 16 chars; rid is 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-] — a control with a malformed/missing rid is still consumed but no result is routed (client times out); at least one of model/effort must be present else empty_request.

sdk_config_result is a transient content frame in the agent_state/typing family: seq'd, never durable, never acked, never replayed, sent only to the requesting device, correlated by rid. Success echoes the accepted post-trim values for exactly the fields the request carried ('' echoes as '' = cleared; absent stays absent) plus restart:true (persisted, supervisor bounce requested) or restart:false (no-op — or, with hot:true, SC6's live apply). Errors carry ok:false and a code from the closed set unsupported_harness|invalid_model|invalid_effort|empty_request|persist_failed|restart_failed plus SC8's hot-path codes unknown_model|apply_failed|no_session|harness_unreachable, with an optional single-line detail <= 200 chars.
a box whose harness is not claude-sdk (the claude TUI, pi, opencode, or an unknown/empty identity) refuses with unsupported_harness and touches nothing on disk.

confirmation closes over the ordinary identity loop: after ok+restart:true the supervisor consumes restart.request, the respawn re-resolves LoadSDK from the updated .env and re-exports HOTLINE_SDK_MODEL/_EFFORT into the child env, and the post-restart welcome (then agent_state / harness_info refinement) carries the new configured values. Caveat, by design: a real-environment HOTLINE_SDK_MODEL/_EFFORT exported by the shell that launched `hotline up` shadows the .env edit (mergedEnv is real-env-wins) — the client surfaces the persistent mismatch.

a model-only request on a hot-capable claude-sdk box hot-applies to the LIVE SDK session: the box forwards sdk_apply to the harness, the harness validates against the CLI's supportedModels() then calls Query.setModel on the live streaming session, restamps harness_info, and confirms; the box answers {ok, model, restart:false, hot:true} — no supervisor bounce, the wire stays up, the harness PID is unchanged. Confirmation is the next agent_state snapshot carrying the new model — no welcome involved. Old app + new box: the unknown hot field is dropped and the old parser treats the frame as a no-op success; the row updates when agent_state lands.

persistence follows confirmation on the hot path: nothing touches .env until the harness confirmed the applied model; every failure leaves .env untouched. NOTE (two-tier guard): 'confirmed' means the harness APPLIED it, not that the catalog vouched for it — a syntactically valid id the catalog does not list is applied and persisted carrying unverified:true, because the catalog under-enumerates live-valid ids and the API is the authority. So a bogus id CAN reach .env on the hot path; what it cannot do is crash-loop the harness, because the session is already running and the rejection surfaces as a next-turn API error the operator recovers from by switching back. Invariant on every outcome: live session model == persisted model, or the client got an explicit error saying which side is ahead (persist_failed after a live apply carries the applied-but-unsaved detail). A respawn therefore never reverts a confirmed hot apply.

hot-path failures are explicit errors, never a silent degrade to a restart: unknown_model (the harness's supportedModels() guard refused — setModel never called, the session doesn't blink), apply_failed (the live setModel control threw), no_session / harness_unreachable (the harness wasn't there to answer / the box's pending budget expired) — all ok:false, session untouched, nothing persisted.

a forwarder-unbound box (telegram-only wiring, older binaries that never bound the hot forwarder) keeps SC3/SC5 restart semantics verbatim for a model OR effort request: it persists, bounces, and answers restart:true. The client supports both the restart and the hot result shapes with no version negotiation.

effort hot-applies exactly like model on a hot-capable box (effort hot amendment): an effort-only (or combined model+effort) request forwards as sdk_apply, the harness applies it to the LIVE session — applyFlagSettings({effortLevel}) for a symbolic level, setMaxThinkingTokens for a raw budget (the same mapping the boot Options use, so a respawn preserves it) — restamps harness_info, and the box persists AFTER the ok and answers {ok, restart:false, hot:true} echoing only the fields the request carried. Confirmation is the next agent_state snapshot carrying the new effort. The hot gate is 'forwarder bound && (model or effort present)'; a combined apply is one restamp and one result.

the harness model guard is two-tier (unverified-model amendment): a syntactically valid model absent from the CLI's under-enumerating supportedModels() catalog is NOT rejected — the catalog is not the truth, the API is. The harness applies Query.setModel anyway (mirrors env, restamps harness_info with the requested id) and answers {ok, model, restart:false, hot:true, unverified:true}; the box persists AFTER the ok exactly like a verified hot apply. unverified is serialized only when true, so verified frames stay byte-identical and old apps drop the unknown field. A truly bogus id sticks here but surfaces as an API error on the NEXT turn, recoverable by flipping back. unknown_model is now reserved for the impossible (setModel-side) case; the ONLY pre-apply model rejection left is the box's syntactic invalid_model (SC2). The client confirms success with a gentle caution instead of the plain success state.
